title: _check_gpu_fallback docstring/contract is false: it refuses (raises) and never falls back to CPU or mutates train_params
description: The docstring states 'Check GPU VRAM; fall back to CPU if insufficient. Mutates *train_params* in-place. Returns updated ram_warning.' The implementation does neither: when VRAM is insufficient it builds a warning, records it on the job, and raises _gpu_vram_http_exception (HTTP 507) — i.e. it REFUSES training rather than silently switching task_type to CPU. It also never assigns to train_params anywhere (it only reads train_params.get('task_type'/'border_count'/'depth') and passes the dict to _check_gpu_vram, which is likewise read-only, lines 361-394). The misleading contract is reinforced by start()'s comment at lines 1093-1095 ('threaded through the GPU feasibility check (which may adjust it in place)'). A maintainer trusting either comment could wrongly assume train_params was mutated (e.g. task_type flipped to CPU) and remove the apparently-redundant reassignment `ram_warning = self._check_gpu_fallback(...)` or mis-handle the refusal semantics.
evidence: Lines 758-794: branch returns ram_warning unchanged when task_type != GPU; otherwise on vram_check.warning it raises _gpu_vram_http_exception (783-788). No `train_params[...] = ...` assignment exists in the function; _check_gpu_vram (361-394) only reads params and returns a _VramCheck. Docstring at 754-757 vs. behaviour, plus start() comment at 1093-1095.
